Lightlark #3

Skyshade

Alex Aster, Diana Morăraşu (Translator)

3.68
133,636 ratings17,342 reviews
Rate this book
Nimic nu este mai periculos decât o inimă sfâșiată în două. Durerea ei poate distruge regate...

Profeția spune că Isla va distruge sau va salva lumea. Dar, odată ce drumul a fost ales, o parte din ea va rămâne pe veci în întuneric, alături de cel pe care l-a iubit. Va putea oare să păcălească destinul care o împinge spre alegeri imposibile?

Adevărul este unul cumplit – nu există cale de ieșire fără vărsare de sânge și fără o iubire arsă de focul trădării. Ziua în care va trebui să înfigă pumnalul nu în trupul unui dușman, ci drept în inima celui pe care îl iubește, este ziua în care va salva regatele, dar își va distruge pentru totdeauna sufletul.

Misiunea ei devine și mai importantă atunci când află că printre supușii ei există un trădător care va încerca să-i pună piedici în cale. Trebuie să îl demaște, dar pentru asta e nevoie să accepte cine este ea cu adevărat și să-și descopere adevărata putere, cheia împlinirii destinului său. Prinsă de dușman în măruntaiele pământului, Isla își amintește cuvintele prezicătorului: „Dintotdeauna ai avut în tine ceea ce-ți face trebuință.” Apoi înțelege:

Din dragoste făcuse cele mai urâte lucruri din viața ei. Dar tot iubirea i-a dat puterea să le facă pe cele mai bune.

Marianna Moore
563 reviews103k followers
November 10, 2024
Ya know… it was fun while it lasted! Honestly I can’t say I’m surprised that this was disappointing for me, I went in with pretty low expectations and they were met.

It was obvious that this series was originally slated as a trilogy and I think this book would have been so much better if it stayed that way. I can’t say I’ll be reading book 4 at this point.

This is gonna be a long one so buckle up… SPOILERS AHEAD!

Starting out with the good, the first half of this book was FOR THE GRIM GIRLIES!!! There were so many Grim and Isla moments that I adored and I was so happy we got more of them! That being said… still not knowing who’s end game is just annoying at this point. It seems like Oro is still in the mix strictly for marketing purposes.

Grimshaw my sweet deadly sad angel of a man, ALL OF THESE TWO STARS GO TO YOU BECAUSE YOU ARE PERFECT AND THIS BOOKS ONLY REDEEMING QUALITY. Every single tab in my book is for Grim. I swear every time this man opened his mouth my clothes mysteriously disappeared. I feel like this book would have been so much better with his POV! I loved seeing him grovel to win back Islas love (though she doesn’t deserve you). The way this man would burn down the world for her and loves every single part of her flaws and claws and all!!! He’s literally perfect nobody can tell me otherwise.

The overall plot in this was just a disaster, honestly the amount of plot holes was comical. In the first two books I really didn’t care that the plot was all over the place because I was so invested in the drama of the love triangle and the romance but seeing as the love triangle made me want to rip my hair out this time around (more on that in a moment), it was way too hard to ignore the issues with the story as a whole. The ending was extremely rushed and just one huge info dump, it seemed like a last minute set up for book 4. It was almost too low stakes, every single issue was very quickly and easily resolved. The magic system also somehow got worse??? Mainly in regards to Islas power. And listen I know this is a low fantasy series I’m not looking for some in depth complex magic system, I just wanted the most basic baseline explanation of how her power worked!!

Honestly though, the worst part about this book was the drawn out, unnecessary love triangle. This is where all my biggest fears about this book came true. It turned into a weak plot device to add unnecessary drama to a story. Now listen is a love triangle my favorite trope? Absolutely not. But when done right, when it’s actually DIFFICULT to choose between two love interests, they add so much angst and are infuriating in the BEST WAY! However a majority of the time they are infuriating in the absolute worst possible way and this book reminded me why I hate love triangles 99.9% of the time.

I don’t care what team you’re on, it is so abundantly clear this entire series that Grim is set up to be endgame, and if that somehow wasn’t clear in the first two books, it’s even CLEARER in book 3. Yet for some reason the love triangle is still drawn out despite Oro being so insignificant the majority of this book. What really bothered me was how 60% of the book we got Isla and Grim rebuilding their relationship and learning how to trust and love each other again with so much emotion and chemistry for it all to just go to absolute shit by randomly bringing Oro back into the mix in the last 30%. All of a sudden we’re back to Islas back and forth NONSENSE because she’s somehow still in love with Oro and so “torn” even though they’ve spent no time together this whole book and have no chemistry whatsoever. Its just so unbelievable it seems like we’ve entirely lost the plot.

The icing on the cake that made me really want to give this 1 star because it made me feel so icky was Isla having sex dreams about Oro and lusting after him while a few days ago she was getting married to Grim a SECOND time, having spicy time with him in every corner of the castle….. honestly I was hurt for Grim so maybe I’m just defensive but at this point she does not deserve him in my mind. Her and Oro can go live in their own delusional world together, preferably at the bottom of the ocean.

Isla girl, you were simply the ✨worst✨ this book did her so dirty, I genuinely am struggling to find any redeemable qualities in her. Zero depth, zero character development, zero regard for the feelings of literally the only two people in her life that care about her. The way she is playing with Oro and Grims emotions made me want to scream. The back and forth repetitive nonsense of “I love them both” “no I love grim” “but I also love Oro” “grims the enemy” “I can’t be around Oro because I’m the villain” “I love grim again we can be villains together” “Grims the enemy again” “but wait Oro…” OH MY GOD SHUT UP. Don’t even get me started on the way she was ready to kill grim for betraying her and then turned around and did the same thing… this girl expects him to be fully truthful with her yet lies to him left and right???

Oro…. Again. You were there. And pathetic tbh. Truly a waste of space.

ALL of that being said, the first two books in this series were so much fun, I had a silly goofy time and giggled and kicked my feet! Just because I didn’t like book 3 doesn’t mean the same will go for you! I’ve seen a lot of people rave about this book and hopefully you’ll love it more than I did!

1.5 stars rounded down

This reviews may contain spoilers we already knew would happen. Read at your own risk ⚠️⚠️‼️

⟢ For the rest of my life, if anyone asks me about my biggest fuck-up, it’s not binge-watching shows instead of studying. Nope. It’s the day I picked up this absolute disaster of a series. The day I let curiosity get me killed, like a damn cat. Every time someone even mentions this book, I swear an angel loses its wings in the most brutal, soul-crushing way possible 🤡. I’m floored—no, fucking floored—that it’s possible to write a book this offensively horrible. I mean, it takes talent to make something this bad.

⟢ Let’s start with the obvious. EVERYONE, their grandmother, their ancestors, and every village idiot from here to eternity knew Isla was going to end up with Grim. So tell me why, in Book THREE, after barely putting in 20% effort for Oro, she’s still dropping lines like, “I love both Grim and Oro,” “Half of my heart belongs to him.” 🤨 EXCUSE ME? I had a damn whiplash every time I read that crap. Is it just shitty writing, or does the author actually think we’re fucking stupid?

⟢ We’re trapped in this girl’s head while she’s with Oro, thinking about Grim, and then with Grim, barely giving a fuck about Oro. Yet we’re supposed to buy this “love them both equally” lie? She’s having a full-on panic attack when she can’t feel Grim but barely bats an eye when Oro is LITERALLY DYING right in front of her. Like…HELLO?! Am I supposed to believe she loves them both? The fuck outta here with that nonsense 🤡.

⟢ Speaking of fuckery, was this book not supposed to be a trilogy? Unless I’m having some kind of brain malfunction, wasn’t this supposed to wrap up? But nooo, we’re getting at least three more of these dumpster fires. Why? To drag out this pointless “love triangle” that’s more predictable than a weather forecast? What’s next? Isla getting god-tier powers…oh wait she fucking did , Grim and Oro still following her like whipped puppies, and some irrelevant plot literally nobody gaf about be fr. I hope all these idiots die and rot. I could not care less 😒.

⟢ And Isla. Holy fuck, Isla. The woman has the personality of an ovulating pig for fucks sake. Bland, boring, and somehow this is the girl they’re all fighting for? Please, for the love of God, STAND UP.

⟢ And Grim. Don’t get me started on this manipulative piece of shit. Every time he does something “cute,” it’s dripping with emotional blackmail. The guy talks about his “nightmares” that only stopped when he met her and how he’s got “no one but her.” I’m sorry, what? This guy is waving red flags like he’s in the goddamn World Cup. It’s giving “my grandma died 15 years ago so I’m a victim” energy. I’m done with this whiny, manipulative fucker 🥰🤡.

⟢ Oh, and the age gap? Jesus Christ. Isla’s dad was Grim’s GENERAL. They had beef back in the day, and now he’s with the man’s daughter? 💀💀 Every time I remember this, I want to puke. The ick is off the charts. YUCK.

⟢ Also Jesus… Grim kills people for even looking at her wrong, and she’s “shocked” that he doesn’t flinch when she says she’s killed people? And then, because he “accepts her darkness,” she likes him even more? DUH, the man’s a murderer himself. This isn’t some cute bonding moment; it’s basic logic. Duhhhhh. 🤡

Reading this reminded me of when I was reading ACOMAF and SJM was shoving Rhysand down our throats like we couldn’t think for ourselves. Somehow this is worseee.

⟢ This whole thing has been a fucking nightmare. I’d go into more detail, but my brain is so fried from this series that I need therapy just to recover.

Grimshaw’s breath stinks, Isla needs to stop begging people to touch her and take a shower , Oro needs to prioritize his sanity and I genuinely from the bottom of my heart hope everyone dies including that stupid fucking dragon, Wraith✌️

Aurevoir, fuck this book, fuck this series, and fuck every bullshit love triangle that drags on for no reason.

*thank you netgalley for this arc—all thoughts are my own.*

➳ 2 ☆

skyshade is the third installment in the lightlark trilogy, and unfortunately this was the worst book thus far. this book picks up immediately after the events of nightbane. we continue to follow isla, grim, and oro, as they navigate this life of love, secrets, and perfidy. while this series has ended on cliffhangers—making the next book a direct continuation of the previous events—this novel emphasizes the cracks and extraneous side quests that are irrelevant to this overall story.

➺ isla : isla is our main character in this series. i was cognizant of what this story entailed especially, pertaining to her character. aster uses a lot of arbitrary plot devices for isla making her a weak lead. in this novel, she continues to explore a way to find a solution to the oracles prophecy, while continuing to lust after both grim & oro. isla was always a very incredulous character, but the jarring nature that was portrayed in this novel was by far the worst aspect of this book. there was not one ounce of inducement for isla's idiosyncrasy. isla has always been a self insert fantasy female lead, however, there was a lot of wasted potential here. she had good qualities to delve into, sadly nothing was explored and she remained the same after three books.

➺ grim : grim is one-half of the love triangle for this series. he was always written as the morally grey + villainous character who kills everyone just for the sake of fulfilling said archetype. while grim is the man i prefer, it does become blaring when the author clearly has favorites. she has always written this series through the scope of ⌞the villain gets the girl⌝ — putting grim on the forefront of this narrative. while there is nothing erroneous about using such facile plot devices, there is no need to market your novels as an “enchanting love triangle”, when the obvious choice has always been exalted. there was a lot of theatrical drama that was redundant and superfluous.

➺ oro : there will always be one character that receives the short end of the stick and this is oro. due to the fact that i am comprehensive that there are a lot of isla + oro shippers, i am unsure why aster did not allow them to go through any real development with each other. if there is a presented trope in which one girl has to choose between killing two of her so called love interests, there needs to be more of an indication and credence to this plot device. while oro is not mundane and futile, he has no genuine reason to be a part of these novels after book one. in addition, he was present in this novel for about ten minutes, and sadly was abrasive and useless the entire duration of his time on page. complete wasted potential on this part.

all in all, there is only so much repetition of comprehensible & stereotypical script that can be displayed. while i am aware this is YA, that does not warrant the novel to be banal and glib. i would recommend checking this out if you have read the first two, but aster herself seems to be unsure of her wants. this book somehow ends with the potential of numerous sequels to follow. there was a decent concept, but average execution.

Overall, I clearly didn’t enjoy it 😭 It was probably a waste of time. Despite all the boring moments and everything that annoyed me, I’m still going to read the next book (I don’t even know why… maybe I just like to torture myself).

Yea, that’s it guys. Love y’all 🫶🖤

I read Skyshade so you don’t have to 🥴

***This review contains spoilers***

Was it good? No.
Did I have a good time? No.
Will I be continuing the series (that’s right, there’s more)? No.
Did we get the answer to the one and only question everyone wants to know? NO!!!

I don’t even know where to start. Tbh, I went into this with low expectations and even those weren’t met.
It’s very obvious this series was originally slated as a YA, low level fantasy. I get that. Even so, it’s so poorly done I could barely get through it.
The world building? Not great.
Magic system? Confusing as hell.
Character development? Lol who?
Plot? What’s that?

ISLA: (Infuriatingly pronounced “Eyez-luh.”) Our FMC born without powers, surprise! She has all the powers! (God I’m getting sick of this trope). I really hoped Skyshade would build on her background to make her a more likable character. Unfortunately, she had the character development of a wet sponge growing mold - predictable, kinda gross, makes you wanna throw it in the trash by the end.
She has zero loyalty to the only two characters who have ever loved her. She does nothing but feel sorry for herself and the fate she’s been given. Infuriating.

Grim: One of two MMC/love interests. Grim honestly carries this entire series on his strong muscly back. All 1.75 stars of it. If you’ve read about one broody, morally grey MMC who is all “touch her and 💀,” you’ve read about Grim. It’s such a stereotype. Don’t get me wrong, it’s one of my favorite stereotypes, but there’s nothing special here. It’s boring and overdone.

Oro: (also infuriatingly pronounced “Are-Oh”) I assume he’s supposed to be the light, morally good opposite to Grim’s dark, morally grey? However his character really has no business in these books past Lightlark. He was on page in Skyshade for like 10 pages and half of that was Isla’s wet dreams of the past. I really wanted to like Oro. I feel like he got the short end of the character development stick.

Speaking of sticks, CAN WE PLEASE TALK ABOUT THE STUPID “STARSTICK?!” Like Aster, come on, “starstick?!?” That’s the best you can do? My brain pictures something between a fairy godmother’s wand with a little glittery star and streamers at the end and Dr. Who’s Sonic Screwdriver. This thing has such immense power and our girl Isla just forgets where she left it like it’s keys to a 1997 Honda Civic.

Anywho, I really wish this book was more of a prequel and less of a continuation of the first two books. When I say it immediately picks up from Nightbane, it’s IMMEDIATE. There is no introduction to help the reader remember what happened in a book that came out more than a year ago.
I would have loved if book 3 was a prequel throwback to when Isla and Grim met/were married before the Centennial. The random flashbacks are not enough for me and it makes the writing so disjointed.

Overall thoughts? A swing and a miss. Three strikes, you’re out, Lightlark. Sorry 🫤.

This series was my first-ever hate read, and wow... what a flaming dumpster fire of chaos 🔥. Normally, I avoid hate reads like I avoid unsolicited spoilers, but this series managed to lure me into its cursed little clutches. Spoiler alert: I read it so you don’t have to. You’re welcome, bookish community. 🙃

Let’s get straight to the point: the love triangle from hell is not just bad—it’s offensively bad. 🤢 Three books deep, and Isla is still doing the emotional hokey-pokey between Grim and Oro? Sweetie, indecision isn’t a personality. PICK. A. STRUGGLE. If I absolutely had to choose (and trust me, I don’t want to), it’d be Grim, simply because he’s memorable in a "toxic ex you keep blocking" kind of way. Oro? Houseplant vibes. And Isla forgiving Grim’s nuclear red-flag behavior? If Grim pulled that nonsense on me, he’d be the main feature in my block list gallery. 🛑

Tropes That Tormented My Soul:
✧ Love Triangle (aka emotional waterboarding) 💔
✧ Broody, overprotective MMC 🖤
✧ “I’m Special Because Plot” Chosen One ✨
✧ Enemies to Lovers (but with gaslighting!) 🔥
✧ Forbidden Romance (forbidden because it’s TOXIC) 🚫
✧ Power Struggles (but make them pointless) 👑
✧ Stuck Between Two Kingdoms (and two brain cells) ⚔️
✧ Prophecies That Nobody Cares About 🌀

Isla: Girl, if emotional depth were water, you’d be a puddle in the desert. Your self-pity and indecision could fuel a dystopian wasteland for decades. Every chapter had me screaming, “JUST PICK SOMEONE AND MOVE ON.” Instead of character growth, she spirals into Chosen One™ mediocrity.

Grim: Oh, Mr. Emotional Blackmail™ himself. Sure, tragic backstory, blah blah blah. But does it excuse his manipulative, red-flag-packed nonsense? Nope. Every “romantic” moment is basically just trauma bonding with a side of guilt trips. 🚩

Oro: Oro who? This man is the literary equivalent of elevator music. He barely exists, and when he does, he’s about as compelling as a chair. Character development? What’s that?

Plot: Wait, there was a plot? Because this “story” felt like a series of irrelevant side quests, unnecessary flashbacks, and twists so predictable I actually rolled my eyes. The pacing was more chaotic than my sleep schedule, and the climax? Straight-up cartoonish. Honestly, it reads like a bad AI bot spat out rejected fantasy fanfiction.

The Bottom Line:
This trilogy was a headache wrapped in a bad decision. Reading it was like voluntarily stepping on Legos—painful and entirely my fault. I hated every second of it, but I guess hate reading has its own masochistic charm. So here’s my official PSA: Save your time, your energy, and your sanity. Don’t be me. 😤

You’re welcome.

╭─ ⋆⋅☆⋅⋆ ───────────── ⋆⋅☆⋅⋆ ─╮
𝐒𝐊𝐘𝐒𝐇𝐀𝐃𝐄 – Alex Aster
★★★☆☆ / 3.5 (strictly Grim-funded rating)
╰─ ⋆⋅☆⋅⋆ ───────────── ⋆⋅☆⋅⋆ ─╯

🎵 “Take Me to Church” – Hozier

✧ third book fatigue ✧ Grim carrying emotional, narrative, and spiritual weight ✧ Isla confusion festival ✧ Oro poetry disease ✧ me here against my will but also emotionally invested ✧

✦ 𝐌𝐘 𝐑𝐄𝐀𝐃𝐈𝐍𝐆 ✦

Let’s be very honest.
I did not read this book for the plot. I read it for Grim.

Everything else was just emotional background noise I had to sit through like waiting for someone to finish a speech they didn’t rehearse.
At this point I’m not “enjoying” this series. I’m just locked in a toxic relationship with it out of curiosity and Grim dependency.

⋆. 𐙚 ˚𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐒𝐓𝐎𝐑𝐘 ⋆. 𐙚 ˚

There is technically a story happening.
It just keeps getting interrupted by emotional spirals, romantic confusion, and characters acting like communication is illegal.

Something important will happen…
and then immediately we cut to someone emotionally overthinking for 40 pages like it’s a full-time job.

✦ 𝐈𝐒𝐋𝐀 °❀⋆.ೃ࿔*:･

★ “I don’t know what I want, but I know I can’t lose either of them.” ★

I need Isla to understand something respectfully.
This is not romance. This is emotional damage with a subscription plan.
She is not torn between two men. She is actively participating in chaos and then acting surprised when it gets messy.

One minute she’s choosing Grim, the next minute she’s mentally window-shopping Oro like he’s a concept instead of a consequence.
At this point she doesn’t need a love triangle, she needs a decision-making support group and maybe a nap.
And I say this with love… but also exhaustion.

✦ 𝐆𝐑𝐈𝐌 ⋆°.☾⋆.ೃ࿔*:⋆
★ “My home is wherever you are.” ★

Yeah.
That’s it. That’s the series.
This man is not a love interest. He is emotional stability with a pulse.

Grim is out here loving her like it’s instinct, breathing like it’s devotion, existing like it’s sacrifice.
And somehow the narrative expects me to accept that this woman is confused? Be serious.

Grim deserves peace. Grim deserves clarity. Grim deserves someone who does not treat his entire existence like a side quest.
If he is not endgame, I will personally write a complaint letter to the universe.

✦ 𝐎𝐑𝐎 ☀︎⋆.ೃ࿔*:･
★ “Meeting you was like remembering what I was like before the curses.” ★

Okay. Let’s talk about poetry on legs.
Oro does not speak, he composes emotional wallpaper quotes.

This man doesn’t act. He narrates.

He doesn’t touch reality, he politely describes it from a distance like it might break if he gets too close.
Every time he speaks, it sounds like he’s auditioning to be a tragic candle scent called “longing and vague suffering.”

Sir… I need actions. I need presence. I need something that is not just beautiful words floating in the air doing nothing.
Right now it’s giving: “emotionally poetic, physically absent.”

✦ 𝐋𝐎𝐕𝐄 𝐓𝐑𝐈𝐀𝐍𝐆𝐋𝐄 ✦
★ Grim: “If I lose you, I lose everything.” ★
★ Oro: “I would burn the world for you.” ★
★ Isla: “I might die if you don’t touch me.” ★

Let’s be real.
This is not a triangle.

This is Grim doing emotional labor at maximum capacity while Oro recites poetry like he’s being paid per metaphor and Isla treats commitment like a loading screen she keeps refreshing.

Grim is fighting for his life and love.
Oro is fighting grammar demons.
Isla is fighting… nothing, apparently.

✦ 𝐇𝐈𝐆𝐇𝐋𝐈𝐆𝐇𝐓𝐒 ✦

✧ Grim being the only functioning emotional adult in the room
✧ Isla making choices like she’s allergic to consequences
✧ Oro speaking exclusively in aesthetic suffering quotes
✧ occasional crying because apparently I care too much about fictional problems
✧ Grim scenes restoring my will to continue
✧ everyone else immediately undoing that progress

✦ 𝐎𝐕𝐄𝐑𝐀𝐋𝐋 ✦

This book is emotionally chaotic, slightly exhausting, and entirely carried by Grim refusing to let the narrative collapse.

The romance situation is messy in a way that feels less like tension and more like confusion with decorative dialogue.

Oro is poetry without presence.
Isla is presence without clarity.
And Grim is the only reason I’m still emotionally invested in anything happening here.

✦ 𝐅𝐈𝐍𝐀𝐋 ✦
★★★☆☆ / 3.5

Strictly Grim-funded rating system.
I did not read this for peace.
I read it because Grim exists.
And honestly?
He deserves better than this entire situation.
wish me luck for the next book
